audit.detail: understand; attempts=1; Build a FastAPI URL shortener backed by SQLite. Users POST a long URL and get back a unique short code. GET /{code} responds with an HTTP 302 redirect to the original URL and records the click. A stats endpoint returns aggregate click counts. No existing files, so this is a new project with top-level Python packages (e.g. app/) and pytest/httpx tests under tests/. Only the preinstalled dependencies are used (fastapi, sqlite3 from stdlib, pytest, httpx).

Use server-generated codes only; no custom aliases. Create a new unique code for every submission, even for duplicate URLs. Store only aggregate click counts, with no per-click timestamps, referrers, or visitor identifiers. Accept only HTTP and HTTPS URLs. Generate seven-character case-sensitive alphanumeric codes using secure randomness, enforce uniqueness in SQLite, and retry collisions with a bounded limit. Use POST /links, GET /r/{code}, and GET /links/{code}/stats.

plan; attempts=1; Plan for a FastAPI + SQLite URL shortener using the clarified endpoints: POST /links, GET /r/{code} (302), GET /links/{code}/stats. An app factory create_app(db_path) in the top-level package `app` makes the DB path configurable (also via the SHORTENER_DB env var). Codes are 7-character case-sensitive alphanumeric, generated with secrets.choice. The links table has code TEXT PRIMARY KEY (UNIQUE) and clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, with no per-click data. Insert uses parameterized SQL and retries on sqlite3.IntegrityError up to a bounded limit (e.g. 10), then returns 500/503. Every submission gets a new code, even for duplicate URLs. URL validation accepts only http/https with a host, via pydantic validation or urlparse, and returns 422 otherwise. Redirect performs a single atomic UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1 WHERE code = ? and checks rowcount for 404, then SELECTs the URL. Tests under tests/ use TestClient/httpx with a tmp_path DB and cover creation, uniqueness, 302 with Location and follow_redirects=False, 404s, click counting, validation, collision retry (monkeypatched generator), retry exhaustion, and code format.
